name: Pasture Stocking Rate Calculator
seoTitle: Pasture Stocking Rate Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: Stocking rate is how many animals a paddock can carry without the grass running out before it regrows. Free pasture stocking rate calculator: enter your value
summary:
Stocking rate is how many animals a paddock can carry without the grass running out before it regrows. It returns usable dry matter, animals carried, livestock units (1 LU = 600 kg cow) and pasture per animal, and the panel shows all of them at once.

It balances pasture supply against intake and grazing efficiency, and gives both the stocking rate and the area each animal needs. The arithmetic keeps full precision internally and only rounds what it displays, so the number you copy out is the number the formula produced. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Pasture Stocking Rate
sections.html:
Animals = (area × yield × utilisation) ÷ (daily intake × grazing days)

sections.title: How do I use the Pasture Stocking Rate?
sections.html:
Fill the boxes you have numbers for; the calculator decides what it can derive from them.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: pasture dry-matter yield of 8,000 kg/ha/yr, utilisation of 65%, daily dry-matter intake per animal of 12 kg/day, grazing days per year of 220 days.

Substituting them into the formula gives usable dry matter of 52,000 kg, animals carried of 19.7 head, livestock units (1 lu = 600 kg cow) of 19.7 LU, pasture per animal of 0.5077 ha/head, pasture area of 10 ha.

Because the example uses the defaults, you can reproduce it by loading the page and reading the results panel before touching anything.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
Interpretation is a convention, not part of the arithmetic. The usual bands are:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
0.8–1.5 LU/haExtensiveunimproved or dryland pasture
1.5–3 LU/haModerateimproved temperate pasture
3–5 LU/haIntensivehigh-rainfall or irrigated, rotational grazing
above 5 LU/haVery intensiveneeds nitrogen, irrigation or supplementary feed

  • Utilisation is the honest number in the equation: of the grass that grows, typically 50–70% can be eaten before the pasture is damaged.

  • Grazing days matters as much as yield — a pasture that is only grazed in summer carries more animals than the same pasture grazed all year.

  • Livestock units let you compare mixed herds: 1 LU is conventionally a 600 kg mature cow.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
Before blaming the formula, check these — they explain nearly every mismatch:

  • Using total grass growth as if all of it were available.
  • Forgetting that stock still need feed when the grass stops growing.
  • Comparing stocking rates without checking whether both are per hectare or per acre.

faq.q: What does the Pasture Stocking Rate actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns usable dry matter, animals carried, livestock units (1 LU = 600 kg cow) and pasture per animal. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
